Sasha: quick heads-up — saw a spike in decode latency for requests that hit function-calls + structured output yesterday on a 2h window :eyes:
Sasha: repro trace attached, looks like batches are fragmenting right at the stop-token boundary and kernel selection falls back to a slower path
Sasha: dump (truncated):
```
[2026-03-16T21:14:02Z] request_id=abc123 batch_id=57 tokens=128 stop_seen=true fn_pause_ms=45
[2026-03-16T21:14:02Z] kernel_choice="fast_path" -> fallback="kv_slow" because sequence_len>96 and tool_pause
[2026-03-16T21:14:02Z] kv_cache_miss=0.42 prefetch=false batch_fragments=3
```
Mike: can you paste the cmd you used to collect the trace? want to repro locally :mag_right:
Sasha: `./tools/perf/collect_trace --id abc123 --window 2h --include-kv --stack`
Sasha: also linked the dashboard: https://redwood.internal/perf/2212 — you'll see spikes at 03:12–03:20 UTC (hosted-dedicated mix)
Priya: hmm. last time we saw similar fragmentation it was due to the queue policy letting tool-invokes block formation while new short requests join the queue — i.e. token_budget_target stayed at 96 which is too high for fnbound flows
Eli: +1. profiling heatmap shows heavy time in kernel selection and kv copy when stop tokens race with function-handshake
Eli: tiny snippet from perf profiler: `chooseKernelForBatch() -> evaluateKVLayout() -> fallthrough to slow_quant_kern`
Jules: do we have telemetry that differentiates "stop inside structured output" vs "fn pause for external tool"? they should be treated differently for batching heuristics imo
Sasha: we do but it's noisy. current heuristics treat any 'stop_seen' or 'fn_pause' as an interrupt and set batch_score=0 which causes immediate flush. that flush + prefetch-miss leads to 2-3 fragments
Mike: idea: if stop token is within the last N tokens of a batch and fn_pause is < X ms, we should bias toward keeping the batch open for short time to let sibling requests coalesce. effectively a short hold-window when stop probability is high but pause is small
Priya: agree. we can try a sigmoid delay: delay_ms = clamp( A * (1 - stop_pos_frac) + B * fn_pause_ms, 0, max_hold ) where stop_pos_frac = position/target_len. empirically we saw 30–60ms should be enough to avoid a fragment in ~70% cases
Eli: also kernel selection fallback is triggered by observed sequence_len distribution per-batch. If we can mark the batch as "likely short end" we can force the fast_path kernel even if seq_len > threshold, with a safety cap on kv memory usage
Jules: risks: forcing fast_path could blow kv memory for some sizes. need a cheap check: if kv_cache_miss_rate < 0.2 and estimated_kv_size < K_LIMIT then allow fast_path override
Sasha: plan proposal: run a canary on one dedicated pool with params:
- token_budget_target: 80 -> 64 for flows with fncall or structured_output
- short_hold_ms: 50 when stop_pos_frac >= 0.75 and fn_pause_ms <= 100
- fast_path_override if kv_miss_rate < 0.2 and est_kv_bytes < 6MB
Sasha: I'll add instrumentation to emit batch_coalesce_reason tag and a small histogram for batch_fragments_per_request so we can quantify impact
InfraBot: deploy-triggered: canary/fast-hold-2212345678 -> started on pool ded-13 at 2026-03-17T02:05:00Z :rocket:
Mike: when you run this, also capture per-kernel token throughput so we can detect regressions if fast_path ends up slower for some shapes
Priya: I'll wire an A/B eval: measure p95 latency, tokens/sec, and token_cost delta over 4h windows. will also log stop_vs_fn_flag to separate flows
Eli: small note — if we reduce token_budget_target we also affect batching for long-running chat sessions (they might create more batches). scope the override to requests with explicit fncall/structured_output header
Sasha: agreed. will gate on header + request_type IN {tool,structured} so generic chat unaffected
Jules: SGTM. also add a fallback kill-switch if kv_miss_rate spikes > 0.4 for > 1m
Sasha: running an initial 2h probe now, will post results. starting with 5% traffic on ded-13 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Mike: thanks — when you post results, include flamegraphs and the batch_fragments histos so we can see before/after
Sasha: will do. last note: saw one regression where structured JSON outputs with many short toolcalls made prefetch worse because our prefetcher assumes long contiguous tokens. added a TODO to make prefetcher aware of tool boundaries
Priya: nice catch. maybe prefetch should be disabled for structured outputs unless kv_miss_rate is low
Sasha: noting that. ok off to run the canary — will update in ~2h :hourglass_flowing_sand:
InfraBot: canary/fast-hold-2212345678 -> 5% traffic on ded-13 (region us-west1) at 2026-03-17T02:07:12Z
Jules: :thumbsup:
